name: Blind Watten
description: Blind Watten (Ladinisch Watten) is a fascinating South Tyrolean variation of the classic Alpine game. In this version, the Schlag (trump rank) and Trump suit are chosen in secret by the forehand and dealer, respectively. Their partners must deduce the trumps through observation of the play alone, as signaling is strictly prohibited. It transforms a lively social game into a high-stakes psychological puzzle of asymmetric information.

history.origins: Originating in the Ladin-speaking valleys of South Tyrol, Blind Watten represents a more disciplined and analytical branch of the Watten family tree. It was developed to test partnership intuition without the reliance on the overt physical gesturing common in Bavarian or Tyrolean Watten.
timeline: 19th Century: Watten spreads through the Alpine regions of the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
Early 20th Century: Blind (Ladinisch) variant solidifies in the South Tyrolean mountains.
Present: Actively played in traditional 'Stuben' and card clubs throughout Alto Adige and parts of Austria.
history.cultural: A symbol of regional identity in the Ladin valleys, reflecting a culture of quiet observation and deep communal trust.
history.evolution: The removal of partner signaling and the introduction of secret trump selection were the key evolutionary steps that defined this variant.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: 33 cards: A, K, O, U, 10, 9, 8, 7 in four suits plus the WELI (6 of Bells).
setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards to each player. Forehand shows a card rank (Schlag) to the dealer in secret; the dealer shows a suit back to forehand in secret.

rules.objective: Win at least three out of five tricks to win the hand. First team to 15 or 18 points wins the match.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Secret Selection**: Forehand and dealer establish rank and suit trumps in secret. 2. **Play**: Forehand leads. **Must Follow Suit** only applies to forehand and dealer for trumps. Partners have no follow obligation but must try to deduce trumps. 3. **The Cards**: Highest card is the 'Guate' (Schlag + 1), followed by the 'Rechte' (Schlag in trump suit), then the 'Linken' (Schlag in the other suit of same color).
keyRules: No signals or verbal communication allowed between partners.
The first trick's cards remain face up on the table to assist in deduction.
WELI is always bells unless 6 is the Schlag.
Betting (raising the stakes) can be done at any time during the hand.

strategy.basic: As the player who knows the trump, use your first play to signal clearly to your partner. If you lead a trump, your partner will likely identify the suit immediately.
strategy.intermediate: Deduction: If your partner (who knows trumps) plays a card and the dealer is forced to follow with a trump, you now know the trump suit. Use this knowledge to support the next lead.
strategy.advanced: The False Signal: Occasionally play a non-trump high card to see if opponents take the bait and assume it's trumps, potentially leading them to waste their own high cards.
tips: Watch the face-up first trick throughout the game.
Don't raise the stakes until you are reasonably certain your partner has identified the trumps.

variations.name: Watten with Kritische
variations.description: Standard Watten where the three top cards (Max, Weli, Spitz) are permanent trumps above the Schlag.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant reintroduces permanent critical trumps, which require additional engine work beyond the base Blind Watten model.

scoring.description: Win 3+ of 5 tricks = 2 points (or higher if stakes were raised by betting). First team to target score wins.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach target score (typically 15 or 18 points).

synthesis.shortDescription: A South Tyrolean partnership trick-taking game where trumps are chosen in secret. Forehand whispers the trump rank to the dealer; the dealer whispers the trump suit back. Their partners must deduce everything by watching the play. No signals allowed. Information is power.
